lines: Stereo feedback delay network reverb with separate decay times for the low and mid bands, high-frequency damping, a pre-delay and a modulated tail
Passes the signal through the reverb when on; with it off the module is bypassed
Sets how long the low band takes to fall 60dB, 0.5 seconds fully counter-clockwise to 32 seconds fully clockwise
Sets how long the mid band takes to fall 60dB, 0.5 seconds fully counter-clockwise to 32 seconds fully clockwise
Sets the frequency dividing the low band from the mid band, 50Hz to 1000Hz
Sets the frequency at which the decay time has fallen to half the MID time, 1.5kHz to 22kHz, so turning it down shortens the top of the tail
Delays the reverb behind the dry signal by 0 to 250ms, which makes the space read as a larger one
Sets how far the modulation moves the decay times, 0 to 100%, from a static tail to a wavering one
Sets the rate of the LFO that modulates the decay times, 0.5Hz to 20Hz
Sets how much reverb is in the output, 0 to 100% wet
Adds to the LOW time knob, where 10V covers the whole of that knob's travel
Adds to the MID time knob, where 10V covers the whole of that knob's travel
Adds to the DAMP knob, where 10V covers the whole of that knob's travel
Adds to the DELAY knob, where 10V covers the whole of that knob's travel
Adds to the MIX knob, where 10V covers the whole of that knob's travel
The left audio input into the reverb
The right audio input into the reverb
The left output, carrying the dry signal and the reverb in the proportion set by MIX
The right output, carrying the dry signal and the reverb in the proportion set by MIX
Note — the reverb algorithm runs at 44100Hz whatever the patch's sample rate, and the module resamples into and out of it
Note — X-OVER, M.RATE and M.AMT have no input jack, so those three take no voltage control
Blamsoft-XFXReverb.notes: Blamsoft publish no source for this plugin; the ranges, defaults and the input-to-knob map were read out of the installed 2.0.2 binary (XFXReverbModule::process and the module constructor's configParam calls). Panel artwork draws a line from each CV jack to the knob it feeds, and the disassembly agrees with every one. Decay times come from a custom ParamQuantity computing 0.5 * 2^(6v) seconds; damping 1.5 * 10^(1.166v) kHz; crossover 50 * 10^(1.301v) Hz; mod rate 5 * 10^(1.6v - 1) Hz; delay and the two percentage knobs are linear. Each CV is added to the knob value at 0.1 per volt and the sum is clamped to the knob's own 0 to 1 range, so the CV cannot push a control past its limits.
